This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the third respondent/insurer in O.P.(MV) No.291/2016 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Kollam (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the Award dated 09/08/2019.
The respondents herein are the claim petitioners 1 to 4 and respondents 1 and 2 respectively in the petition.
Cross objection No.104/2022 has been filed by the claim petitioners seeking enhancement.
In this appeal and cross objection, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.
2. The claim petitioners are the parents and siblings of deceased Sethu Krishnan.

According to the claim and Cross Objection No. 104 of 2022 2025:KER:73582 petitioners, on 03/10/2015 at 09:45 a.m., while the deceased was riding motorcycle bearing registration no.KL-23-H-4478 near Geetha Krishnan vs Sbi General Insurance Co Ltd on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26543635/
4

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Vellayittambalam junction, tipper lorry bearing registration no.KL-23-G-1990 driven by the second respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down, as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries to which he succumbed.
3. The first respondent/owner and the second respondent/driver remained ex-parte.
4. The third respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the policy but denying negligence on the part of the second respondent.
The averments in the petition regarding age, occupation and income of the deceased were disputed.
The compensation claimed under various heads was contended to be exorbitant.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts.A1 to A15 were marked on the side of the claim petitioners.
No documentary evidence was produced by the respondents.
and Cross Objection No. 104 of 2022 2025:KER:73582 6.

The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the second respondent-driver of the offending lorry resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 26,24,800/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.

Aggrieved by the Award,
the third respondent/insurer has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal and cross objection is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides.
9. The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following head is challenged- Notional income

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the third and Cross Objection No. 104 of 2022 2025:KER:73582 respondent/insurer that when the income claimed in the claim petition was 10,000/- only, the Tribunal was totally unjustified in fixing the notional income at 16,500/-.
Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioners that the amount that has been fixed by the Tribunal is quite reasonable and that it does not call for any interference.
9.1. Going by the allegations in the claim petition, the deceased was earning 10,000/- per month.
This Court as per judgment dated 12/09/2025 in MACA No.721 of 2020 has fixed the notional income of a painter in the year 2015 as 15,000/-.
Hence, the notional income of the deceased herein can also be fixed as 15,000/- in the absence of any other materials on record to prove the claim regarding income.
9.2. The claim petitioners have also filed cross objection.
However, on going through the impugned award, I find that reasonable amounts have been awarded under all the other heads.
Hence, I find no ground for interference.
